APPLICATION

Turn noisy samples into a useful signal.

128 outputs per variant. Zero integer mismatches.

Host stores coefficients and sample history. MAC8 performs the arithmetic. The 16-tap filter introduces a 7.5-sample group delay. Plot values are from simulation; no physical throughput is claimed.

ARCHITECTURE

One multiplier. A precise contract.

Host
samples + coefficients
→
MAC8
8 × 8 → sat24
→
Readback
3 bytes

The host supplies signed operands over an 8-bit bus. A synchronized strobe accepts commands. Sticky overflow records saturation. The output register exposes the selected accumulator byte.

Driver and bring-up guide →
CYCLE EXPERIMENT

Three commands per fresh pair

364 cycles / FIR output

LDA → LDB → MAC. Includes CLR and full readback.

Same one-clock setup, three-clock strobe, three-clock low interval. 50 MHz assumed. Software GPIO overhead is excluded.

Local mapping adds 1.28% cell area. Routed cell area adds 1.48% under identical flow configuration, PDK and source commit. Both meet setup and hold across nine corners, with zero DRC, LVS and antenna errors and 15/15 prechecks. Transition violations remain. The candidate needs a separate waiver review before adoption.

VERIFICATION

Prove the scope. Break the protections.

  • Exhaustive signed multiplication and exact FIR references.
  • Both saturation rails, sticky overflow, byte reads and reset recovery.
  • Nine application tests and 100,000 operations pass on the hardened candidate.
  • Fused scheduling invariants pass BMC and induction, with reachable covers.
  • Old-B, missing-MAC and stuck-low busy mutants are caught.
  • A missing pending-reset mutant fails the control proof.

Formal scope covers scheduling and selected handshake properties. Arithmetic equivalence and physical metastability are outside those proofs.
